title: Common Problems
markdown:
| Problem | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reading a child's output never finishes | the parent still holds the pipe's write end | close your copy right after `CreateProcessW` | 1.04 |
| Parent and child both hang | both blocked writing to full pipes | read each output pipe on its own thread or with overlapped I/O | 1.04 |
| A child keeps a file or pipe open unexpectedly | it inherited every inheritable handle | use `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST` | 1.02 |
| Helper processes survive the main program | not in a kill-on-close job | add them to a job with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` | 1.03 |
| Messages arrive merged or cut in half | a byte stream has no boundaries | frame messages with a length prefix | 2.03 |
| Client gets `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` | the server is not running, or a different pipe name | start the server; compare names | 2.02 |
| Client gets `ERROR_PIPE_BUSY` | every instance is in use | `WaitNamedPipeW` and retry; create more instances | 2.04 |
| Memory corruption with overlapped I/O | the `OVERLAPPED` or buffer went out of scope while pending | keep them alive until completion | 2.05 |
| Shared data is garbage in the other process | a pointer or `std::string` was stored in shared memory | store offsets and fixed-size data | 3.02 |
| A reader sees half-updated state | torn read | seqlock or double buffering | 3.05 |
| `CreateMutexW` fails with `ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE` | another kind of object already has that name | use distinct names | 4.01 |
| A consumer sleeps although data is waiting | lost wakeup; event reset after the data arrived | drain all work after each wake; time out waits | 4.02 |
| A wait returns `WAIT_ABANDONED` | the mutex's owner died while holding it | validate or repair the shared data | 4.03 |
| `WM_COPYDATA` never arrives | the receiver runs elevated (UIPI) | `ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx` in the receiver, or use a pipe | 4.04 |
| Two processes hang waiting for each other | lock-order or request-reply deadlock | global lock order; no locks held across IPC; timeouts | 4.05 |
| Firewall prompt when the app starts | the server bound to `0.0.0.0` | bind to `127.0.0.1` | 5.01 |
| A web page can trigger your local API | localhost has no access control | token, Host and Origin checks | 5.05 |
| A worker restarts hundreds of times | no backoff on a crash loop | exponential backoff and give up | 6.02 |
